content: This domain was evaluated exclusively in cluster-randomized studies. The risk of bias due to loss of clusters, incorrect analysis, and compatibility with individual randomized controlled trials (RCTs) was deemed unclear and not applicable to the studies reviewed. Study: Daly 1996 Methods: A double-blind, randomized cohort trial with two arms. Participants: The study included 567 children aged 6–8 months living in an inner-city area of Birmingham. Only children whose mothers had already transitioned their diet to unmodified cow's milk (n=116) were invited to participate. Interventions: A total of 100 children were randomized into two groups. Group 1 (n=40) received fortified milk, while Group 2 (n=40) continued with cow's milk. Parents were compensated monthly to purchase the milk. At 18 months, infants on fortified milk were transitioned back to cow's milk, and developmental assessments were conducted at enrollment, 18 months, and 24 months. Funding: The study was funded by Farley Health Products. Risk of Bias: Random sequence generation: Low risk, as randomization was performed using blocks of four. Allocation concealment: Low risk, with blinding maintained except for one field researcher. Baseline outcome measurements: Low risk, with no significant differences in hemoglobin concentration, mean corpuscular volume, or serum ferritin between groups at baseline. Baseline characteristics: Low risk, with no significant differences in demographic or socioeconomic factors between groups. Incomplete outcome data: Unclear risk, as some data points were missing due to illness, inability to locate participants, or insufficient blood samples. Blinding of participants and personnel: Unclear risk, as the study was reported as double-blinded, but it was unclear if participants could distinguish between interventions. Blinding of outcome assessment: Unclear risk, as this was not explicitly mentioned. Selective reporting: Low risk, with ethical approval obtained. Other biases: Unclear risk, as no additional biases were identified. Study: Ghisolfi 2012 Methods: A non-randomized, cross-sectional controlled study with two arms. Participants: The study included 713 children aged 15 days to 36 months from various regions of France. For the study's purpose, only children aged 12–24 months (n=132) were included. Interventions: Children were divided into two groups based on milk intake: Group 1 (n=63): Consumed at least 250 mL of cow's milk daily. Group 2 (n=55): Consumed at least 250 mL of follow-on formula daily. Outcomes: The study measured daily energy and nutrient intake, including macronutrients, essential fatty acids, vitamins, and minerals. Funding: The study was funded by the French Association of Baby Food Industries. Risk of Bias: Random sequence generation and allocation concealment: High risk, as randomization was not used. Baseline outcome measurements and characteristics: Unclear risk, as these were not reported. Incomplete outcome data: Low risk, with transparent documentation of participant flow. Blinding of participants and personnel: High risk, as the study was not blinded. Blinding of outcome assessment: High risk, as blinding was not implemented. Contamination: Low risk, as children continued their usual milk consumption. Selective reporting: Unclear risk, as ethical approval was not required under French legislation. Other biases: Unclear risk, as no additional biases were identified. Study: Gill 1997 Methods: A randomized controlled trial conducted across multiple centers with three arms. Participants: Healthy term infants aged six months were recruited from 21 centers in the UK (n=192) and Ireland (n=214). All infants were receiving formula or cow's milk at entry. Interventions: A total of 406 infants were randomized into three groups: Group 1 (n=264): Received iron-fortified follow-on formula. Group 2 (n=85): Received unfortified follow-on formula. Group 3 (n=57): Continued with cow's milk (reference group). Both formulas were provided free of charge, and mothers in the cow's milk group were compensated for milk expenses. Outcomes: Anthropometric and laboratory measurements were conducted at 9–10 months, 12 months, and 15 months of age. Funding: The study was funded by SMA Nutrition, with formulas provided by Wyeth Laboratories. Risk of Bias: Random sequence generation: Low risk, with randomization performed on a 3:1 ratio. Allocation concealment: Unclear risk, as this was not mentioned. Baseline outcome measurements: Low risk, with no significant differences in weight, length, or head circumference at entry, though hemoglobin values differed between Groups 1 and 3. Baseline characteristics: Low risk, with well-balanced randomized groups. Incomplete outcome data: Low risk, with reasons for withdrawal documented. Blinding of participants and personnel: High risk, as no blinding was reported. Blinding of outcome assessment: High risk, as no blinding was reported. Contamination: Unclear risk, as this was not addressed. Selective reporting: Unclear risk, with ethical approval obtained. Other biases: High risk, as statistical analyses were conducted by Wyeth Laboratories. Study: Lovell 2018 Methods: A double-blind, multicenter randomized controlled trial with two arms. Participants: Healthy one-year-old children (n=160) from Auckland, New Zealand (n=108), and Brisbane, Australia (n=52). Interventions: Participants were randomized into two groups: Group 1 (n=80): Received 300 mL of reduced-protein follow-on formula (GUMLi). Group 2 (n=80): Received 300 mL of unfortified cow's milk. Dietary intake was assessed at baseline and at 3, 6, 9, and 12 months post-randomization. Outcomes: The primary outcome was body composition, with secondary outcomes including micronutrient status, anthropometry, and cognitive development. Funding: The study was funded by Danone Nutricia Research. Risk of Bias: Random sequence generation: Low risk, with computer-generated randomization stratified by study center. Allocation concealment: Low risk, with independent preparation of the randomization list. Baseline outcome measurements: Low risk, with no baseline differences between groups. Baseline characteristics: Low risk, though differences in fathers' employment status were noted. Incomplete outcome data: Low risk, with minimal exclusions documented. Blinding of participants and personnel: Unclear risk, as the study was reported as double-blinded but lacked details. Blinding of outcome assessment: Unclear risk, as this was not explicitly mentioned. Selective reporting: Low risk, with no evidence of selective reporting. Other biases: Unclear risk, as no additional biases were identified. This detailed summary provides a professional and comprehensive overview of the studies, their methodologies, interventions, outcomes, and potential biases.
